In this approach, we will estimate the forecasting model using observations at times 1, 2, ..., k+i-1 for i = 2,...,T-k, where T is the total number of observations. The forecast error for each step is computed for k+i. This process is repeated for i = 2,...,T-k to obtain a series of forecast errors.

Next, we will compute the forecast accuracy by omitting the first observation (i = 1) and repeating the above step for i = 1, 2, ..., N, where N is the total number of observations. This process will provide another series of forecast errors.

By using this method, we make efficient use of the available data as only one observation is omitted at each step for time series data. The forecast accuracy measures, such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), or Mean Squared Error (MSE), can be computed based on the errors obtained from both series.
